steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook pasta in boiling water until al dente; drain.

Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat; add onion and garlic, and cook until golden brown. Mix in tomatoes, mushrooms, and spinach. Season with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes. Cook 2 minutes more, until tomatoes are heated through and spinach is wilted. Reduce heat to medium, stir in pasta and feta cheese, and cook until heated through.

raw_recipe.headline: Suki's Spinach and Feta Pasta
raw_recipe.description: Penne pasta mingles with onion, garlic, tomatoes, mushrooms, wilted spinach and feta with a dash of red pepper flakes for zip.
raw_recipe.name: Suki's Spinach and Feta Pasta

review.reviewBody:
I have been making this recipe for many years now and it still remains my all time favorite! One thing I can't stress enough...you MUST use a GOOD quality feta. The kind you get in a grocery store just doesn't have enough flavor. I'm lucky enough to have a Greek deli nearby that offers excellent feta. I also double the amount of spinach and always add extra garlic and red pepper flakes.
If you'd like it a bit more hearty, try adding chicken tenderloins, cut up and sauteed.

Thank you for a great recipe. Add 2 TBSP chopped Kalamata olives and 1 TBSP olive juice for acid balance. 2 more cloves of garlic is about right. Contrary to other reviews, DO NOT add salt unless you taste it first - there is plenty already in the feta. Great on a ridged whole grain penne. Cook pasta until 90% done and finish off when you add to the sauce.

I needed an easy but attractive dinner for 15 people, and this dish was a hit! (My 22-month-old granddaughter ate as much as some of the men!) I premeasured everything into large bowls so that at cooking time, all I had to do was dump in ingredients. (If you double the recipe, make sure to use two large skillets instead of one.) I'm glad I took others' suggestion and doubled the spinach and increased the mushrooms. Delicious with a big salad and herbed rosemary bread. This will become one of my go-to meals for both company and everyday. Thanks, Suki!

This is a great and very versatile recipe. I made some changes: I added a teaspoon of balsamic while the mushrooms were cooking, quadrupled the amount of spinach and wish I had put more. Also added bell pepper and some kidney beans I needed to use. Came out great! The feta give everything a wonderful taste, and I didn't add salt because feta is already salty.

This is a good base recipe, but I wish I had listened to the other reviewers about using good feta. I tried to be healthy and use fat-free feta, and I think it REALLY affects the taste. No matter how much red pepper and salt/pepper I added, I just felt like something was missing. Next time, I'll make sure to use a full-flavored, full-fat Greek feta; I think that will help give it more flavor.

Also, I more than doubled the amount of spinach (6cups) and still felt like I could have used more. I forgot how quickly spinach leaves shrivel up when cooked. I could probably bump it up to 8 cups next time - more spinach is always a good thing!

Edit:
- Measured 16 oz of uncooked pasta and it made an entire saucepan full
- Used 8 cups of spinach and thought it was just the right amount
- Used 4 cups of tomatoes
**I think what was crucial in giving it extra flavor this time was using a full-fat, "Crumbled Feta with Mediterranean Herbs" from Trader Joe's. The pasta was a lot more flavorful this time.

Fantastic recipe! Followed others advice and increased garlic, onion and used a combination of fresh, canned diced and grape tomatoes. My own personal modification was to use frozen five cheese ravioli in lieu of the penne pasta which made this an exceptionally tasty and filling vegetarian meal. My teenage son went back for four helpings. Yum!

We really liked this recipe. I made some very slight modifications- I added the crushed red pepper to the onions and garlic so it would infuse into the oil a little bit (we like spicy food!), then when the onions were almost done I threw in about a pound of shrimp. As soon as both sides turned pink, I threw in the rest of the vegetables. If you like spinach, I would recommend adding a whole bag- 2 cups looks like a lot but cooks down to less than half! The feta added a great creamy consistency. A great dish!

Very flavorful easy recipe. I used whole wheat linguine, canned diced tomatoes (didn't have enough fresh ones), and more spinach than the recipe called for. I put 3 cups in initially and then put another handful right before serving. Next time I will wait until the very end to put the feta in so it doesn't melt as much. Didn't have red pepper flakes but was still great without it. Definitely making this again.

Excellent... I always read the reviews... added medium size cooked/peeled shriimp as another reviewer suggested and then sprinkled freshly grated parmasean cheese when serving...served for a ladies night dinner went over really well. The little bit of leftovers were fabulous the next day too.

Wow, this is so simple and tastes like a million bucks! I used one 15 oz. can of diced Italian style tomatoes (drained) because tomatoes are out of season. It was the perfect amount of tomatoes for me. Since I'm a vegetarian and need a little extra protein, I added some toasted walnuts just before serving. I’ve also made this using chevre in place of feta, adding a splash or two of milk with great results.

This meal was very good...... I did change it around to make it basically...FAT FREE!! So, I gave this recipe a 4 star with my changes to the recipe. I didn't use any olive oil...I used Olive Oil Spray (PAM)...and I also used fat free feta cheese. I took the advice of others...and added more spinach...(doubled it)..I may triple the spinach next time...cause it wilts to nothing... My husband loved it too...may add chicken next time. I made it again..a few days later...and just ate it plain without any pasta!!! Delicious!!
I have been using this recipes for years, I can't believe I haven't made it in awhile! Dinner tomorrow ☺️

I added sun-dried tomatoes, extra spinach and cherry tomatoes. I find it extremely bland. I put plenty of salt and pepper in it. Not sure what to do now. Did not like it at all. Really muddy taste and not pretty at all. Yuck!
I doubled the garlic. I doubled the onion. I did not put in the pepper flakes. I added toasted pint nuts. Loved it!
Not enough spinach. I added more spinach, peppers, white beans and a little tomato sauce. Also added the feta on the individual servings so we used a lot less cheese.

Nice, easy recipe! I personally added some extra garlic, which was great. I can see this being a good base for adding other veggies, olives, and protein as desired. I bet it would be good with chicken or sausage.
I added a little pasta water and a tablespoon of cream cheese to the pasta mixture. It blended well with the feta and made for a slightly richer taste!
Husband and daughter loved this recipe! Added extra garlic and spinach, along with chicken… topped with shredded Parmesan cheese. Very good! Adding to the rotation… thank you Suki! :)
So easy and delicious. I did add chicken with the onions for a little bit extra

This is an AMAZING meal. I did add chicken breast chunks to make it more heartier, changed the chopped tomatoes to sliced sundried tomatoes, took out the mushrooms since my kids don’t like them and added onion powder and garlic powder for extra flavour. Everyone in the house loves it and I now make it regularly.
